summary: US-023a: A seat map can be marked orphan-preventing (setting only, nothing enforces it yet)
description:
**First of four slices carved out of TKT-175** when its plan showed the ticket to be ~50 files across five services. The architecture is decided — see TKT-175's `kind=plan-final`.

Ships the **decision** and the **setting**, and nothing that acts on either.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] **ADR-041** records the arbitration decision: geometry fetched once at provisioning for the exact immutable published version (ADR-029), projected into inventory, decided under the pool lock. It states why a claim-path catalog call (ADR-010), a new `seat_map.published` subscription, and a commerce pre-check were each rejected — the last because an advisory check cannot satisfy a contention AC.
- [ ] `seat_maps` gains `orphan_prevention_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; a guarded Down refuses while any map has it on.
- [ ] Catalog's create/read/edit contract carries it. An edit that omits it **inherits the predecessor's value**; an explicit value applies only to the newly minted version (ADR-029: versions are immutable).
- [ ] The back-office venue page can set it on create and on edit.
- [ ] **Nothing reads it.** No event payload changes, no inventory change, no claim behaviour changes. Every existing map and every existing test behaves exactly as before.
- [ ] Spec declared, generated code committed before the gate, browser evidence for the back-office form submission (the repo's rule: an unsubmitted Astro form is unverified).

Quality gates: `make check` green; browser submit evidence.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` ... Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: The architecture, every design decision and the full test plan live in TKT-175's kind=plan and kind=plan-final — read those first, they are not repeated here

governingAdrs.why: A published seat-map version is immutable and an edit mints a new one. That is why the setting is per VERSION and why an edit's omission must inherit rather than reset — and it is the property the whole TKT-175 architecture rests on.
Contract-first: the catalog spec changes and openapi_gen.go plus api-types.gen.ts are committed before the gate.
The migration runs out-of-band as the service's migrate subcommand; the server path never migrates.

### ✅ Readiness — PASS

Smallest possible slice: a decision and a flag nobody reads. Its whole risk surface is the migration default and the edit-inheritance rule, both of which are directly testable.

Shaping is inherited: TKT-175's `kind=plan` (gpt-5.6-sol) and `kind=plan-final` (main-agent) decided the architecture, the design, the test plan and the risks before this ticket existed. This child re-scopes delivery, not thinking.
